guide.google_drive.name: Google Drive
guide.google_drive.step1: Open drive.google.com, choose New → File upload and pick the vault file.
guide.google_drive.step2: Right-click the file and choose Share → Share.
guide.google_drive.step3: Add the recipient's Google address (best). Otherwise set General access to Anyone with the link.
guide.google_drive.step4: Choose Copy link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.onedrive.name: Microsoft OneDrive
guide.onedrive.step1: Open onedrive.live.com, choose Add new → Files upload and pick the vault file.
guide.onedrive.step2: Select the file and choose Share.
guide.onedrive.step3: Enter the recipient's Microsoft address (best), or set the link to Anyone can view.
guide.onedrive.step4: Choose Copy link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.dropbox.name: Dropbox
guide.dropbox.step1: Open dropbox.com, choose Upload → Files and pick the vault file.
guide.dropbox.step2: Hover over the file and choose Share.
guide.dropbox.step3: Invite the recipient's email address (best), or create a link with view access.
guide.dropbox.step4: Choose Copy link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.icloud.name: Apple iCloud Drive
guide.icloud.step1: Open icloud.com/iclouddrive, or the Files app, and upload the vault file.
guide.icloud.step2: Select the file and choose Share → Collaborate or Send copy.
guide.icloud.step3: Under Share options, choose Only invited people and add the recipient's Apple address (best), or Anyone with the link.
guide.icloud.step4: Choose Copy link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.synology.name: Synology (Drive / QuickConnect)
guide.synology.step1: Sign in to Synology Drive through your QuickConnect address and upload the vault file.
guide.synology.step2: Right-click the file and choose Share.
guide.synology.step3: Give the recipient a user account on your NAS and share with it (best), or set Privacy to Anyone with the link can view.
guide.synology.step4: Make sure the link uses https, copy it and paste it into the link field here.
guide.synology.step5: Keep the NAS running and QuickConnect enabled for as long as the switch lives.
guide.nextcloud.name: Nextcloud
guide.nextcloud.step1: Open your Nextcloud, go to Files, choose + New → Upload file and pick the vault file.
guide.nextcloud.step2: Open the sharing panel of the file.
guide.nextcloud.step3: Share with the recipient’s Nextcloud account or email (best), or create a share link, ideally with a password you give them separately.
guide.nextcloud.step4: Copy the link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.gmx_webde.name: GMX / WEB.DE Cloud
guide.gmx_webde.step1: Sign in to GMX or WEB.DE, open the Cloud and upload the vault file.
guide.gmx_webde.step2: Select the file and choose Share.
guide.gmx_webde.step3: Invite the recipient by email (best), or create a link for reading.
guide.gmx_webde.step4: Copy the link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.proton_drive.name: Proton Drive
guide.proton_drive.step1: Open drive.proton.me and upload the vault file.
guide.proton_drive.step2: Select the file and choose Share.
guide.proton_drive.step3: Invite the recipient's email address (best), or create a public link.
guide.proton_drive.step4: Copy the link and paste it into the link field here.
guide.own_server.name: My own server
guide.own_server.step1: Copy the vault file to your web server, into a folder that is served over https.
guide.own_server.step2: Give it a name that is hard to guess, or protect the folder with a login you give the recipient.
guide.own_server.step3: Open the address in a browser to check that the file downloads.
guide.own_server.step4: Paste the https address into the link field here, and keep the server running for years.
guide.usb_paper.name: USB stick or paper
guide.usb_paper.step1: Copy the vault file to a USB stick (two sticks are safer than one).
guide.usb_paper.step2: Print the paper backup for this recipient and put it with the stick.
guide.usb_paper.step3: Give both to the recipient, or put them where they will look: a drawer, a safe, a notary.
guide.usb_paper.step4: Leave the link field empty; the release email will say to open the vault you gave them.

privacy.intro: What this site knows about you, for how long, and how to make it forget.
privacy.browser.title: In your browser only
privacy.browser.text: Your letters, their key and the vaults exist only in this browser's memory and in the files you download, and, if you choose, in your owner archive, which is encrypted with your passphrase. No analytics, no tracking, no third-party scripts, no fonts from elsewhere.
privacy.messenger.title: What the messenger stores
privacy.messenger.text: Only if you use it: your email, your recipients' names, emails and languages (encrypted at rest), the switch's public record, and each share link encrypted with a key nobody has before release, the operator included. It never holds the key of your letters before release and never sees a letter.
privacy.retention.title: For how long
privacy.retention.text: Until 30 days after the last email of a released switch, 7 days for a fire drill; a cancelled switch is deleted at once. Afterwards only a note remains that the switch existed (network, identifier, final state, dates), so it cannot be registered twice. Addresses that chose "never" are kept only as a keyed hash.
privacy.delete.title: How to delete it
privacy.delete.text: Cancel the switch in My switches, or delete its data at the messenger with your owner code (Messenger settings), or use the stop link in any email.
privacy.operator.title: What the operator receives
privacy.operator.text: The organiser fee, as an ordinary payment, and through the messenger the email addresses you chose to give. The operator cannot read, delay, open or cancel a letter, and cannot read a link before release.
privacy.none.title: Spam and abuse
privacy.none.text: A switch must exist on the chain before the messenger accepts it. A recipient's first email only asks to confirm; addresses have limits and can say "never"; fire drills only email confirmed addresses.
